−27 [[Bryson DeChambeau]] (2021)}} | current_champion = {{flagicon|USA}} [[Scottie Scheffler]] | pushpin_map = USA#USA Maryland | pushpin_label = Caves Valley GC | pushpin_caption = Location in the [[United States]]##Location in [[Maryland]] | pushpin_relief = yes | pushpin_map_size = 240 | coordinates = {{coord|39.451|-76.744}} }} The '''BMW Championship''' is a professional [[golf]] tournament which is the penultimate [[FedEx Cup]] playoff event on the [[PGA Tour]] schedule. Introduced in [[2007 PGA Tour|2007]], the BMW Championship was previously known as the [[Western Open]]. The [[Western Golf Association]], which founded and ran the Western Open, runs the BMW Championship. In 2012, 2013, and 2014, the [[PGA Tour]] named the BMW Championship its Tournament of the Year.{{cite press release |url=https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/usa/pressDetail.html?title=2013-bmw-championship-earns-pga-tour%25E2%2580%2599s-tournament-of-the-year-honor&outputChannelId=9&id=T0160644EN_US&left_menu_item=node__5122 |title=2013 BMW Championship Earns PGA Tour's Tournament of the Year Honor |publisher=BMW Group |date=October 12, 2013}} The BMW Championship is the longest running regular [[PGA Tour]] event on the calendar outside of the four major tournaments. ==Western Open== {{for|a detailed history of this event, including a list of its champions|Western Open}} The [[Western Open]] was first played {{Years or months ago|1899}} in 1899. For many years, the Western was played in and out of the state of [[Illinois]], before eventually settling down in the [[Chicago area]]. The [[Western Golf Association]] (WGA) ran the Western Open throughout its entire history (1899–2006), and continues to run the tournament under its new title. These are, however, two entirely different events in terms of playing format and invitational criteria. The Western Open was like any other regular PGA Tour stop – although it was once considered to be one of golf's majors. The BMW Championship is part of the [[FedEx Cup#How the FedEx Cup works|FedEx Cup Playoffs]], and only the leading [[FedEx Cup]] points earners at the start of the BMW event are eligible to play. ==Tournament format== {{for|a detailed explanation of the FedEx Cup Playoffs|FedEx Cup}} The BMW Championship is open to the leading [[FedEx Cup]] points earners on the PGA Tour following the [[FedEx St. Jude Championship]]. Through 2022, the top 70 players were qualified, after which it was reduced to the top 50. With a limited field, there is no 36-hole [[cut (golf)|cut]]. The top 30 in the FedEx Cup points list following the BMW Championship advance to [[The Tour Championship]], where the FedEx Cup champion is decided.{{cite web |url=http://www.pgatour.com/fedexcup/fedexcup-overview.html |title=FedEx Cup 101 |publisher=PGA Tour |access-date=September 7, 2014}} ==Winners== {{also|Western Open#Winners}} {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:95%" !Year!!Winner!!Score!!To par!!Margin of
